newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends at day's highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends at day's highs.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures made fresh gains on Monday afternoon and nearby months finished the day at session's peak, helped by a run-up in New York and worries over cold weather in Brazil's coffee belt.
Traders said the advance also reflected an upward technical adjustment after last week's big sell-off that wiped out prices by almost one-third on the week.
"I think this is a technical reaction to the downside," said one trader. "The market may be trying to build a base around this area."
"The big sell-off had forced out most weak long holders. The strong ones are probably those who bought below these levels and nobody wants to go short due to Brazil frost scares," he added.

The market gapped higher as expected but then lost some ground on overhead trade and origin sales. But the upside momentum gathered strength in the afternoon on early rise in New York on weather-related buying.
Front-month July was $67 up at $1,890 by the finish after a low of $1,831. September regained a foothold above $1,900 and ended $75 up at $1,925.
Activity was less brisk and overall turnover stood at a modest 4,641 lots. Active July/Sept spread widened to $35 from $25 on Friday.

Another bitterly cold night is in store for Brazil's coffee areas on Monday but any frosts are expected to be limited to lower-lying areas where coffee is not grown, Brazilian weather forecasters say.
Brazilian cooperative officials and coffee growers in the country's coldest coffee regions said on Monday they had not heard of any frosts on coffee farms.

A cold airmass which brought chilly temperatures to the country's coffee belt this past weekend is expected to move out to the Atlantic and bring in warmer weather during the next week, Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said on Monday. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
